comments.body:
Ah, ok, I see. Interesting! Yea, so the `Sender` stored inside the h1 dispatcher gets dropped like normal when the whole future is dropped, and the inner channel just triggers that it is closed. While the receiver side could be smarter and notice if a length had been advertised, in cases where it wasn't, that probably shouldn't be considered a clean close.

One option is to adjust the `Dispatcher` to store the `Sender` in some sort of drop guard, such that any drop while in it triggers sending an unexpected error. The dispatcher already takes the body out and puts it back in if there's still more to do, so it wouldn't change much there. Would just need care that there aren't any other code paths that don't take the sender but should in that case.
Nice! Yes, your summary sounds correct.
